result.title: AMARIS: Merging Generalist and Specialist LLMs via Adaptive Subspace Inheritance
result.summary: Domain specialization of large language models (LLMs) often improves target-domain performance but degrades broad capabilities. Model merging is an attractive training-free alternative, yet common parameter-space strategies (for example, interpolation and sparsified averaging) provide limited control over task-specific interference. We introduce Adaptive Model Alignment via Ranked Inherited Subspaces (AMARIS), a covariance-driven framework that transfers specialist updates only along selected activation directions. AMARIS formulates merging as budgeted subspace inheritance: it seeks high specialist activation capture under a regularized base-output perturbation budget, then builds a low-rank projection gate from ranked generalized eigendirections. This yields a single static merged checkpoint that concentrates transfer in high-utility, low-interference directions. We evaluate AMARIS on Qwen3-based merges (8B and 32B) across finance, instruction-following, and multilingual SEA specialization. In our evaluated settings, AMARIS reaches Pareto operating points that are competitive with strong training-free baselines, including 98.37% specialist retention with 95.16% core retention for the 8B finance setting, 103.55% core retention with 90.28% specialist retention for the 8B instruction-following setting, and 99.20% core retention with 94.80% specialist retention for the 32B SEA setting. These results support subspace-constrained merging as a practical route to compositional capability integration without additional training.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 AMARIS，把专家 LLM 的合并表述为「预算受限的子空间继承」：在限制对基座输出扰动的正则约束下最大化专家激活捕获，用协方差驱动的广义特征方向排序构造低秩投影门，产出单一静态合并 checkpoint，并在 Qwen3 8B/32B 的金融、指令跟随、多语言 SEA 场景评测。
AI.relevance_reason: 与 LVR 主线无直接关联，但其「高任务效用、低干扰」的秩化子空间选择思路，可能为向 VLM 内部状态注入视觉证据时控制干扰、避免核心能力坍缩提供可供核查的方法线索。
